<description>
Before eae193e750235e4023b3e6313284eede2cd7a022, Connect() only started the connection and returned true. If tor wasn't running the refusal was reported later and only logged under -debug=tor. Since eae193e750 (in v32), every failed reconnect attempt logs:

```
2026-11-04T14:14:08Z connect() to 127.0.0.1:9051 failed after wait: Connection refused (111)
2026-11-04T14:14:08Z [warning] tor: Error connecting to address 127.0.0.1:9051
2026-11-04T14:14:08Z [warning] tor: Initiating connection to Tor control port 127.0.0.1:9051 failed
```

On a default configured node without tor, this pollutes debug.log with 18 lines every hour.

This makes the following improvements:
- Log connection failures as warning if tor config is explicit set (`-torcontrol`, `-torpassword` or `-listenonion`), otherwise at debug level.
- Log at info level when an active onion service is lost.
- Log info at the first tor connection failure if no tor config is explicit set.

The first two commits are from @fjahr.
</description>

[2026-11-06] c:6674882387 comment by fjahr (member) (edited 2026-11-07):
I agree that the current behavior isn't ideal but it seems that an bigger problem than noisy logs is that you wouldn't see any logs unless you had `-debug=tor` if you had `-torcontrol` set explicitly, i.e. you clearly want to use Tor but there is an issue and it doesn't work. That's why I think the current v32 behavior was an improvement to the previous behavior. Instead of reverting, I would suggest a more complete fix that works well for both scenarios: When the user configured Tor they should see logs and when they didn't they should not see them (only with `-debug=tor`).

I have drafted the change so people can decide if they like this more: https://github.com/fjahr/bitcoin/commits/2026-11-torlog/ But note that this also includes a bit of additional improvements like making the logging less noisy when it does happen and deals with losing the connection along the way.
